title: TSMC employee data breach involving cloud provider infrastructure
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company confirmed a personal employee data breach exposing 6.9GB of information allegedly stolen through a compromised cloud provider.
takeaways: ~46,000 TSMC employees affected; third-party cloud provider compromised
Exposed data: addresses, bank account numbers, emergency contact information on 499 employees (sample)
Attacker claimed 6.9GB of files; demanded ~$200,000 (3 bitcoins) ransom
TSMC confirmed no breach of own systems or customer data; breach limited to employee records via cloud provider

title: FAA issues ground stop due to communications disruption
summary: The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop November 14 due to a communications disruption affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers nationwide. No cyberattack evidence has been found, though the FBI was investigating. The underlying cause remained unclear as of the latest update.
takeaways: Nationwide ground stop issued November 14 citing extraordinary circumstances
Communications issue impacted all Air Route Traffic Control Centers nationwide
No cyberattack evidence found; FBI investigating
Inbound international flights handled case by case
Cause of communications disruption remained unclear

title: Muji operator discloses security breach exposing customer credit card data
summary: Ryohin Keikaku, Muji's operator, disclosed a November 12 security breach exposing over 1 million credit card records. Full 16-digit card numbers of expired, canceled, and active cards were compromised due to unencrypted, improperly protected data that should have been deleted. A credential-stuffing
takeaways: Affected 1+ million customers who signed up for Muji Card by July 2021
Full 16-digit card numbers of expired, canceled, and valid cards exposed
440,000 additional cash-on-delivery customers may have been exposed
Credential-stuffing attack using unrelated breach data; card data never encrypted or properly protected
Muji suspended online store and app functions; reopening date undecided

title: CISA Adds UnrealIRCd Server Vulnerability to Known Exploited Flaws Catalog
summary: CISA added CVE-2026-114713, a high-severity command injection flaw in UnrealIRCd, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 14 following active exploitation. The vulnerability allows any network user to inject server commands with server authority; patching was mandated for federal
takeaways: CVE-2026-114713: UnrealIRCd versions 6.0.0 before 6.2.7.1; CVSS 8.6
Flaw: improper neutralization of IRCv3 'label' message tag in labeled-response module
Enables command injection executed with server authority on networks with 2+ linked servers
Fixed in v6.2.7.1 released Nov 7, 2026; exploitation began ~1 day after hotfix
FCEB agencies must patch by Nov 16, 2026 (BOD 26-04)
